ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer to decide whether the 12:49–12:55 off-route segment (F3) counts or is exempt; if it counts, issue a RydeTAXI metered refund of 3.52 km × $1.4099/km = $4.96, otherwise $3.12 for the 13:07–13:13 segment only; keep the $0.11 waiting unit and the 0.77 km corridor residual charged.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the distance line moves with the metres driven and RD-2's metered branch applies rather than the fixed-quote branch [F8][RD-2]. Two off-route segments are recorded: 12:49–12:55 adding 1.31 km (F3) and 13:07–13:13 adding 2.21 km (F4); each must be reviewed separately under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F3][F4][RD-1].

RD-4 excuses neither segment: no traffic incident was recorded near the route in the trip window (F15), so RD-4(a) fails, and the only speed records are band 5 (40–49 km/h) on the CTE and Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 (F13, F14), not the band 1–2 that RD-4(b) contemplates, with fair weather (F16) [F15][F13][F14][F16][RD-4].

For segment F3 the rider's only pre-segment message is F10 ("Sure, go ahead.") at 12:47, answering the driver's 12:46 ask to go round the jam "via Serangoon Garden Way" (F9) — words that name a specific road, so the consent is a named-road agreement, not a general route choice [F9][F10][RD-5]. No record ties the driven 12:49–12:55 path to Serangoon Garden Way: the GPS fact names no road (F3), the traffic facts name only the CTE and Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3 (F13, F14), the complete timestamped chat (F11) has no locating message, and nothing places the segment elsewhere; the driver's post-trip statement (F12) is not rider consent [F3][F13][F14][F11][F12][RD-5]. Both advocates state the same ground — named_road_untied — which yields undetermined (G13), and that undetermined finding changes the refund amount, so the case must go to a person [F3][RD-5].

For segment F4 the rider's last message is 12:47 (F10), twenty minutes before the 13:07 segment, with nothing in the chat agreeing to it (F11); the driver's own statement concedes the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting (F12) [F4][F10][F11][F12][RD-5]. On the stipulated ground consent_after_or_none this segment counts: 2.21 km × this trip's rate ($33.02 ÷ 23.42 km = $1.4099/km) = $3.1159 → $3.12 [F4][F5][RD-2]. If F3 were held to count, the formula gives 3.52 km × $1.4099/km = $4.96 [F3][F4][F5][RD-2]. Because the F3 finding is undetermined, the amount is not determinable here. The residual 0.77 km on the $6.05 excess-distance line is corridor/loop and map-matching noise, not refundable [F5][F3][F4][RD-2], and the $0.11 metered waiting unit (F6) stays chargeable under RD-3(c) [F6][RD-3].

RD-6 does not engage: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (F18), so no prior route finding exists and no account flag is warranted [F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: Rider's 12:47 'Sure, go ahead.' (F10) answers the driver's 12:46 ask to go round the jam 'via Serangoon Garden Way' (F9), so the consent is to a named road only [RD-5]. Nothing ties the 12:49–12:55 driven path to Serangoon Garden Way — F3 names no road, F13/F14 name only the CTE and Ang Mo Kio Avenue 3, and the complete timestamped chat F11 has no locating message — and nothing places the segment elsewhere; per G13 the tie is undetermined, so under RD-5 the segment is neither exempt nor counted, and because this changes the refund amount the case goes to a person [F3][F13][F14][F11][RD-5].

The only rider message is 12:47 (F10), twenty minutes before this 13:07–13:13 segment; the complete chat (F11) contains no rider agreement covering it, and the driver's post-trip statement that the second turn-off was his 'GPS rerouting' (F12) is a driver claim, not rider consent [F4][F10][F11][F12][RD-5]. With no rider message before the segment agreeing to it, the segment counts as an unexempt off-route segment under RD-2 [RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The $4.96 figure adds the F3 segment's 1.31 km to F4's 2.21 km, but the only rider consent (F10) is a named-road agreement to Serangoon Garden Way with nothing tying F3's driven path to that road, so F3 is undetermined under RD-5/G13 and cannot be added to the refund by this ruling [F3][F9][F10][F11][F13][F14].
RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1; the record shows route: 0 among the driver's upheld matters (F18), so the 'repeated' condition is not met and no flag_account attaches [F18][RD-6].

The $6.05 excess-distance line covering 4.29 km cannot be refunded in full: RD-2 refunds only unexempt segment extra_km, and the 0.77 km residual beyond the segments is corridor/loop and matching noise expressly excluded [F5][F3][F4][RD-2].

Correct that the $6.05 line is not wholly refundable, but the refund cannot be limited to 'unexempt segments' totalling 3.52 km, because the F3 segment's 1.31 km is undetermined and excluded from this ruling, leaving 2.21 km as the settled non-exempt mileage [F3][F4][F5][RD-2].

The driver's reading of RD-6 is partly wrong: there is a refundable deviation finding (F4 counts), but RD-6 still fails because route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (F18), so no account flag is warranted [F4][F18][RD-6].
